key_points: GDPNow jumped to ~5% for Q3 and the FOMC describes activity as solid with strong productivity and AI capex: real growth is accelerating, not slowing.
Initial claims at 197k (below a year ago) and sentiment rebounding from lows point to resilient demand despite soft June payrolls (+57k); the July jobs report on Aug 7 is the key 1w risk.
Strong growth supports earnings and tight credit spreads, giving a modest upward tilt for equities and a slight tightening bias for HY spreads.
Growth strength with a hawkish-leaning Fed (three hike dissents) keeps a mild upward bias on 2y and 10y yields, though yields are already at 1y highs and much is priced.
Growth lens gives little edge on oil, gold, breakevens and the dollar; VIX near the low end of its range limits further downside.
Core PCE ~3.3% y/y but June m/m only ~0.13%; June CPI headline fell 0.4% m/m on energy — near-term prints softening at the core level.
WTI rebounded ~22% in July, so July headline CPI (mid-August) likely firmer; supports breakevens modestly near term, from a low 32nd-percentile level.
Fed hawkish tilt: 3 dissents for a hike, easing bias removed, 'will deliver price stability' — keeps front end supported, though much is priced with 2y near 1y highs.
10y at a 1-year high with long-run expectations anchored and staff projecting disinflation into 2027; slight mean-reversion lean over 3m.
Oil's supply-shock premium fading after Hormuz agreement implies energy-driven inflation pressure should ease over 3m, mild downside lean for crude.
Initial claims at 197k are near cycle lows and well below a year ago (218k); unemployment ticked down to 4.2%, so the labor market is stable to slightly tightening.
June payrolls +57k as published is soft, but claims argue against a weak July report (likely released in the 1w window); a solid print reinforces the hawkish tilt.

With three FOMC dissents for a hike and the statement saying job gains keep pace with the workforce, firm labor data raise front-end hike pricing: mild upside for the 2y and a flattening bias in 2s10s.
Steady employment plus 4.95% GDPNow supports earnings and tight credit spreads; modest positive tilt for equities, slight tightening bias for HY OAS.
Wage growth (AHE 3.4%) is not an inflation driver, so labor gives little signal for breakevens, oil or gold; those stay near 0.50.
Yields already sit at 1y highs and edges are small; the labor view tilts directions but does not override the market baseline.

The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% with three hawkish dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) favouring a hike; the easing bias has been dropped and the statement says it 'will deliver price stability'. Policy bias is now toward firming.

The 2-year at 4.28% sits about 65bp above the effective funds rate, so a meaningful hiking path is already priced. Further 2-year upside needs a hawkish September SEP or hot data, while the June CPI decline pulls the other way. Near-neutral.

The 2-year fell 5bp and the 10-year rose 6bp in the FOMC week, a bear steepening. The 10-year sits at its 1-year high, driven by term premium. A Fed perceived as credible on inflation caps breakevens and long-end inflation risk premium, so I lean slightly against further 10-year gains over 3 months.

A hawkish Fed is partly offset by hiking ECB/BoE and the dollar's recent softening. Dollar-index futures speculative positioning sits at its 52-week high (99th percentile), which limits dollar upside.
Equities have strong earnings/AI support and solid growth (GDPNow ~5%), so the upward drift is intact. A hawkish Fed tilt is a headwind but not a regime break.
Gold is pressured by higher real rates and the hawkish tilt. Oil is falling back after the Hormuz agreement. Breakevens are anchored by Fed resolve.
The September 16 SEP and dot plot are the key event risk inside the 3-month horizon. That argues for a slight upward tilt in VIX and HY spreads from low levels.

Early-August quarterly refunding is the near-term fiscal catalyst; with strong growth, elevated deficits and AI-related corporate issuance competing for duration, the risk is toward steady-to-larger coupon supply and continued term-premium pressure.

The last week's bear steepening (10y up 6bp while 2y fell 5bp) is a term-premium signature; the Desk flagged the shift from price-insensitive official holders to price-sensitive private buyers, which supports a modest steepening bias in 2s10s.

10y yields are already at the 1-year high, so supply-driven upside is partly priced and mean reversion tempers conviction; 2y is driven by Fed hike odds (three hawkish dissents) rather than supply, so it is near neutral.
Term-premium-driven yield increases tend not to support the dollar the way rate-differential moves do, and fiscal concerns offer mild support to gold after its 14% 3-month drop.
Higher long-end yields are a headwind for equity valuations and a mild upward risk for VIX and HY spreads from low levels, but the strong earnings and growth backdrop limits the effect.
Financial conditions are loose: NFCI at -0.55 and easing slightly. HY OAS is tight at 2.85 and VIX is about 16, which keeps carry and risk assets supported.
The Fed balance sheet is roughly flat at $6.74T, with reserve management bill purchases keeping reserves ample. Repo traded soft, up to 15bp below IORB in May. No funding stress is visible.

The hawkish tilt is the main tightening risk: 3 dissents for a hike, the easing bias was removed, and the 'will deliver price stability' language. That caps further easing of conditions and keeps front-end hike risk alive.

The 10y at a 1y high of 4.75 reflects term premium as ownership shifts toward price-sensitive private holders. Heavy spec shorts in TY futures (20th percentile) raise squeeze and mean-reversion risk, so there is a slight lean lower in 10y yields.

Spreads are near historic tights and private credit redemptions are rising, which leaves modest widening risk at 3m. Lower-income households lean on credit and small-business credit is tight, but there is no near-term catalyst.
Dollar spec longs sit at the 99th percentile and are crowded, offsetting rate-differential support, so the dollar view is neutral. Liquidity-driven support favors equities modestly at all horizons.
Dollar index spec net long at 99th percentile of 52 weeks is a crowded trade, and the dollar already slipped 0.8% last week; contrarian tilt lower.
10y yield sits at a 1-year high with speculators heavily short TY (20th pct). The duration short is crowded, so a squeeze or mean reversion risk modestly favors lower 10y yields.
2y specs covered shorts (99th pct net, i.e. least short), leaving little positioning fuel. Hawkish dissents offset that, so roughly neutral.
VIX at 16 (23rd pct) after a 2.6-point weekly drop, with VX shorts trimmed; complacency argues for mild upside skew in vol and slight HY spread widening from tight 2.85%.
ES net positioning is the least short in a year, but outright exposure is small; positive equity drift still dominates, with a modest bullish tilt.
Oil specs added 38k longs right as price fell 6% in a week, a late-long risk; gold positioning is mid-range with price near 1-year lows, a slight rebound bias.
Dollar fell ~1% over the past month even as US 10y yields rose 31bp — a sign that rate differentials are no longer driving the dollar.
Speculative long-dollar positioning in DX futures sits at the 99th percentile, so the setup is crowded and vulnerable to unwinding.
ECB and other AFE central banks are hiking or signaling hikes, while the Fed holds at 3.50-3.75. Narrowing short-rate differentials argue for modest further dollar weakness.

Global sovereign yields are being pushed up by foreign tightening, and price-sensitive private holders are replacing official buyers of Treasuries. This supports term premium and a steeper 2s10s, though the 10y is already at its 1y high.
Hormuz reopening and the Iran MOU removed the energy-shock premium, and oil fell 6% on the week. Weaker foreign growth in Europe and Asia ex-high-tech caps oil demand.
A softer dollar and strong AI-driven Asian export demand mildly support US equities and gold. Credit spreads and VIX are near benign levels, with limited global catalysts until the September FOMC.

WTI at $86 after a +22% July re-escalation spike and a -6% week; the range of $55-115 shows extreme geopolitical volatility, with speculative longs jumping 38k contracts — crowding plus likely backwardation roll-down tilts spot modestly lower over 1-3m.
Hormuz-related supply disruptions are the key upside tail; the June US-Iran agreement precedent shows de-escalation can collapse prices quickly, so skew is two-sided but the drift leans down.
10y breakevens track oil; with oil expected to ease and the Fed hawkish (3 hike dissents), breakevens are tilted slightly lower.
Gold is at the 6th percentile of its 1y range after -14% over 3m; rising real yields and a hawkish Fed cap the rebound, so it is near neutral to slightly bearish.
Energy pass-through keeps headline inflation elevated, supporting front-end yields, but a fading oil impulse limits further 10y upside from the 1y high.
Equities are supported by the AI capex boom and solid growth; commodity-driven risk is mainly a volatility tail, with VIX at a low level leaning modestly up over longer horizons.

The Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz remain the dominant geopolitical driver. The US-Iran MOU and the reopening agreement have only partly held. Oil rose 22% over the month but fell 6% last week, which points to two-way headline risk.
The fragile ceasefire skews oil and breakevens slightly lower on further normalization. A tail risk of renewed escalation keeps this close to even.

The run-up to the November midterms falls inside the 3m window. Midterm-year seasonality historically lifts volatility into September and October. Low VIX (~16, 23rd percentile) argues for VIX upside and slightly wider HY spreads.
Gold is near its 1-year low after the risk premium unwound. That leaves cheap optionality on any re-escalation, so there is a mild upside tilt.
Rates are at 1-year highs, with three hawkish dissents in favor of a hike. Geopolitics adds a modest downside tilt to 10y yields through safe-haven flows and lower oil if the de-escalation holds.
Equities are supported by the AI capex boom. Geopolitical and election noise tempers the 1m view, but the 3m drift stays mildly positive.

thesis: Growth is solid: GDPNow near 5%, claims at 197k, AI capex strong and financial conditions loose. That supports a persistent upward drift in equities, strongest at 3m. The Fed has turned hawkish, with three hike dissents and the easing bias dropped, but the 2-year is already priced well above the funds rate. The 10-year sits at its 1-year high with crowded spec shorts, so I lean slightly toward mean reversion lower over 1-3m despite term-premium and supply pressure; 2s10s is neutral. The dollar faces crowded long positioning and AFE central banks that are hiking, so I lean mildly lower. Oil should fade its supply-shock premium after the Hormuz agreement, though escalation is a two-sided tail risk; breakevens drift slightly lower with it over 3m. Gold is near neutral, with cheap optionality offset by high real rates. VIX at 16 and tight HY spreads leave mild upside skew into the September SEP and midterm-season volatility. Edges are kept small and close to the playbook-weighted consensus.
